issues.legal_issue: A grant made for the benefit or support of a religious institution is not a grant on service tenure merely because the institution is religious, and does not qualify for the assessment exemption applicable to service-tenure inams.
material_facts: The land was acknowledged in a title deed as a religious endowment or institutional inam held for the support of a religious institution.
The grant’s purpose was not known, but the inam register presumed it had been conferred for the institution’s benefit.
The title was confirmed to the institution’s manager for the time being and his successors.
The revenue authority levied full assessment on the land under the inam assessment legislation.
issues.conclusion: The statutory proviso for inams granted on service tenure did not apply to the land; it was liable to full assessment.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 3(1) of the Madras Inams (Assessment) Act, 1956, the proviso exempts an inam granted on service tenure, proved to consist only of an assignment of land revenue. A grant to an institution as such is distinct from a grant attached to an office or made to an individual burdened with service, and is not a service-tenure grant. Grants for worship or religious observances have been treated as grants to the institution, not as service inams. The Court applied Subramania v. Kailasanatha, AIR 1934 Madras 258, and Hindu Religious Endowments Board, Madras v. Thadikonda Koteswara Rao, AIR 1937 Madras 852. The Act’s object of imposing full assessment on previously exempt or partly exempt inam lands informs the construction of “service tenure”; classifications in the Board of Revenue’s Standing Orders and section 44B of the Madras Hindu Religious Endowments Act, 1927, did not alter that construction.

rule.if: inam_assessment_case and grant_for_institution_support and not grant_burdened_with_service

predicates.inam_assessment_case: The proceeding concerns assessment of land held under an inam grant.
predicates.grant_for_institution_support: The grant was made for the benefit or support of a religious institution as an institution.
predicates.grant_burdened_with_service: The grant was made to an office or an individual and burdened with service to be performed by its holder.
predicates.land_subject_to_full_assessment: The land is liable to full assessment.

issues.definition: When an inam assessment proceeding concerns a grant made for an institution’s support rather than a grant burdened with service, the land is liable to full assessment.

issues.legal_issue: A generally applicable land assessment does not violate the right of a religious denomination to own and administer property when the burden is shared in the same manner by landowners generally and is not specially imposed on the denomination.
material_facts: The assessed land was held by a religious institution.
The assessment was a burden shared in the same manner by landowners in the State, rather than a special burden imposed on the religious institution.
issues.conclusion: The imposition of assessment did not violate Article 26 of the Constitution.
issues.legal_principle: Article 26 protects a religious denomination’s right to own and acquire property and to administer it in accordance with law. A general land-assessment burden shared in the same manner by all landowners is not a special burden on a religious denomination and falls outside the protection asserted against such an assessment.

rule.if: religious_property_assessment_case and burden_shared_with_landowners_generally and not special_burden_on_denomination

predicates.religious_property_assessment_case: The proceeding challenges an assessment imposed on property held by a religious denomination.
predicates.burden_shared_with_landowners_generally: The assessment burden applies in the same manner to landowners generally.
predicates.special_burden_on_denomination: The assessment imposes a burden specifically on the religious denomination rather than landowners generally.
predicates.assessment_does_not_violate_denomination: The assessment does not violate the denomination’s constitutional property right.

issues.definition: A generally shared assessment on religious property does not violate the denomination’s property right when it is not a special burden on the denomination.
